question: Which of the following elements has three shells with two valence electrons?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Magnesium (Mg)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** is a chemical element with an atomic number of **12**.
 
• The electronic configuration of Magnesium is **2, 8, 2**, meaning it has **three shells**, with the outermost shell (valence shell) containing **two valence electrons**.
 
• Magnesium belongs to the **alkaline earth metal group** (Group 2) in the Periodic Table.
 
• It is a lightweight metal and an essential element for life, playing a critical role in biological systems such as **chlorophyll in plants**.
 
• Magnesium is known for its **high strength-to-weight ratio**, making it useful in industries like **aerospace, automobiles, and electronics.**
 
• In its natural state, Magnesium occurs in minerals like **dolomite and magnesite**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorine (Cl)**__

 __
 
• **Chlorine** is a non-metal element with an atomic number of **17**.
 
• Its electronic configuration is **2, 8, 7**, meaning it has three shells but **seven valence electrons**, not two.
 
• Chlorine is a member of the **halogen group** (Group 17) and is highly reactive.
 
• It is widely used in **disinfectants, bleaching agents, and water purification processes.**
 
 
 
• **Silicon (Si)**__
 __
 
• **Silicon** is a metalloid with an atomic number of **14**.
 
• Its electronic configuration is **2, 8, 4**, meaning it has four valence electrons, not two.
 
• Silicon is a major component of **sand and quartz** and is extensively used in **semiconductors and electronic devices.**
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus (P)**__
 
 
• **Phosphorus** is a non-metal with an atomic number of **15**.
 
• Its electronic configuration is **2, 8, 5**, meaning it has five valence electrons, not two.
 
• Phosphorus is essential for **DNA, RNA, and ATP production** in living organisms.
 
• It is commonly found in **phosphate rocks** and is used in fertilizers.
